items.title: Survey reveals the toolbox item your phone is most likely to replace
items.summary: Hint: It isn't the hammer.
items.body: Credit: Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority As a childhood Trekkie, Captain Picard’s tricorder was second only to the holodeck as the technology I hoped to have when I grew up. Well, we’re basically there, and then some. Your smartphone might not be able to take vital signs in as much detail as the hallowed Starfleet tool, but then I don’t remember Geordi La Forge listening to Spotify or booking a hotel on the tricorder. But amazing as our devices already appear, you might not even realize all the tools your phone’s sensors can replace. After we laid some of them out, we were keen to find out which one you might actually consider using. We recently looked at five examples of what your phone’s sensors can do , including using the device as a tape measure, a metal detector, a spirit level, or a sound/light meter. The fifth was a thermometer, but since it’s a Pixel-exclusive tool that’s been ditched on the Pixel 11 , we left it out when we asked in a poll which of the other four jobs you’d actually use your phone for.

items.title: Flo Rida Performs With a Baby During Philadelphia Phillies Postgame Concert
items.summary: The hitmaker turned Citizens Bank Park into his house.
items.body: Flo Rida had Philadelphia’s Citizens Bank Park rocking for his Phillies postgame concert — and he got an unlikely assist from a sleepy baby in the crowd. The Philly faithful stuck around to rock with Flo Rida after the 6-4 win over the Miami Marlins on Tuesday night (Aug. 18). The 46-year-old ran the gauntlet of his smash hits, moving from the field to the stands and ending up in the dugout. While performing an a cappella version of his top five Billboard Hot 100 hit “My House” from atop the dugout, Flo Rida picked up a baby from an eager parent in the audience, which made for a hilarious moment. Fitted in a baby Phillies jersey, the toddler seemed to be woken up from a nap with the speakers booming throughout the stadium. Flo Rida held the baby in one arm while rocking the mic in his other hand and gave the kid a kiss on the cheek before handing her over to the parents. items.summary: As consolidation leads to fewer big movie releases, multiplexes are looking to Taylor Swift, Beyoncé, BTS and more to help fill seats.
items.body: In the fall of 2023, Taylor Swift briefly became not just the biggest star in music, but the biggest star at the multiplex. That October, Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour opened to $93 million at the North American box office over its opening weekend, stunning the film business and helping kick off a new wave of theatrically released concert films. Importantly, it also arrived amid a sparse theatrical release calendar due to the overlapping writers’ and actors’ strikes, making it a godsend for movie theaters that were starved for content. In this way, it showcased the important role concert films can play for film exhibitors, which are increasingly looking to alternative content as the number of major studio releases declines and audiences stay home to stream from their couches. items.title: Samsung fixes Instagram One Hand Operation glitch

items.body: Credit: Zac Kew-Denniss / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has confirmed that One Hand Operation doesn’t work with the Instagram app. One-handed gestures fail due to incorrect settings of the gesture exception area. Samsung recommends updating to version 9.2.21, which fixes the problem. For anyone with small hands, Samsung’s One Hand Operation is a great feature. As the name suggests, it lets you navigate your phone with a single hand using simple, comfortable gestures. However, the popular Good Lock module has been causing some trouble lately . The latest instance was causing conflicts with the Instagram app, but a fix is available. On Samsung’s community forum , a Galaxy user who frequently uses One Hand Operation says they are having issues with the Instagram app. The user claims that One Hand Operation does not take priority when overlapped on Instagram. As a result, swiping gestures only navigate through Instagram’s tabs.

items.title: Google built a camera-based tool to estimate body fat more accurately than wearables
items.summary: Google’s PhotoScan AI turns simple phone photos into surprisingly accurate body fat readings.
items.body: TL;DR Wearables can estimate body fat using bioelectrical impedance analysis, but really accurate readings require X-ray scans. Google Research shares a new technique for delivering high-quality estimates based on selfies. Beyond just breaking down body composition, the system could also be used to predict insulin resistance. Most of us have a weight problem. According to the NIH , almost 3 out of 4 American adults (73.1%) are either overweight or obese. But getting the full picture of your body composition is a whole lot more complicated than just stepping on a scale , and some of the most accurate ways to assess how and where we carry fat rely on complicated X-ray analysis. Some Google researchers have been working an easier way to offer that same sort of insight, using little more than the cameras on our phones. PhotoScan is Google Research’s system for estimating body composition by using AI to analyze a series of 2D images of your body. items.title: Pixel 11 can search your whole Google account right from the app drawer
items.summary: A new search experience on Pixel and Galaxy Z Fold 8.
items.body: TL;DR The Pixel 11 series comes with a new utility called Pixel search. Pixel search expands the capabilities of the phones’ app drawer search bar, allowing users to surface additional information like photos and emails. While Pixel search is updated through the Play Store, it’s currently only available on Pixel 11 phones. The search bar that lives in Pixel phones’ app drawers has long been able to search for more than just apps, and on the new Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro , it can help you find even more stuff. Google’s latest phones upgrade system-wide search with the ability to find specific photos, files in Google Drive, and more. That enhanced functionality comes courtesy of a new app appropriately called Pixel search . Pixel search comes preinstalled on Pixel 11-series phones. We saw hints of the new software in an Android 17 beta this past spring , but now that some customers have received their Pixel 11-series phones, Pixel search is out in the wild — and interestingly enough, the app is also showing up on Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Z Fold 8 Ultra, as noted by Droid Life .

items.title: Sony’s WH-1000XM4 revival finally shows its face, with a notable upgrade in tow
items.summary: Leaked images show the WH-1000XM4C in its new color options, and we get Bluetooth 6.0 for good measure.
items.body: Credit: Adam Molina / Android Authority TL;DR New images give us our first proper look at Sony’s upcoming WH-1000XM4C headphones. The revived model reportedly upgrades to Bluetooth 6.0 while keeping the familiar XM4 design. Sony also appears to trim battery life and NFC, helping it hit a lower expected price. We’ve known for a couple of weeks that Sony plans to bring back the much-loved WH-1000XM4 as the cheaper WH-1000XM4C. Now we can finally see what that comeback looks like, and the first official-looking images arrive alongside some new details about what’s changing under the hood. Roland Quandt of WinFuture has published images of the WH-1000XM4C in black, lavender, and white. That last colorway was previously reported as Platinum Silver, but it looks pretty white to us. Given the popularity of the original headset, Sony hasn’t really rethought its six-year-old design, as the new headphones look almost indistinguishable from the originals apart from the fresh finishes.

items.title: Google’s rolling out an AI-themed visual tweak for paid accounts
items.summary: Google's new colors are blue and purple.
items.body: TL;DR Google is rolling out a new graphic for accounts with paid Google One and Google AI subscriptions. A new ring in a blue and purple gradient is appearing around Google profile images, replacing the old four-color ring. Google seems to be on a mission to fill its software with as many visual reminders of Gemini as possible. Google recently launched new Gemini integration for Chrome on Android that adds a prominent Gemini button to the browser’s UI. Now, users on Google’s paid AI plans are starting to see a new, Gemini-themed effect appearing around their Google Account profile pictures. We saw this new effect in development in June . Now, as spotted by 9to5Google , some customers on Google’s paid subscription plans have started seeing a Gemini-themed, blue-and-purple ring replace the standard four-color ring that’s denoted a Google One subscription for some time now. Subscribers on lower-tier plans are also being nudged to upgrade to Ultra.

items.body: الجناح الفرنسي كان أحد أبرز نجوم "النمور" في العامين الماضيين أصبح الفرنسي موسى ديابي، جناح الاتحاد، أقرب من أي وقت مضى من مغادرة النادي خلال فترة الانتقالات الصيفية الحالية، بعد حدوث تطور مفاجئ في مستقبله. وقال الصحفي السعودي ماجد هود إن نادي باير ليفركوزن الألماني دخل في مفاوضات متسارعة مع الاتحاد، من أجل ضم موسى ديابي في الميركاتو الصيفي الجاري. وأوضح الصحفي السعودي، في تغريدة عبر حسابه الشخصي على موقع "إكس"، أن الجناح الفرنسي سيغادر قلعة "النمور" بنسبة كبيرة، حتى إن الاتحاد بدأ في البحث عن بديل له. باير ليفركوزن دخل في مفاوضات مع الاتحاد لضم ديابي منذ بداية سوق الانتقالات الصيفية الحالية ، غير أن تلك المفاوضات توقفت بشكل كبير خلال الفترة الماضية. تذاكر مباريات دوري روشن السعودي اشترِ تذكرتك الآنَ! ويلعب ديابي لصالح الاتحاد منذ صيف 2024، عندما انتقل إلى صفوفه قادمًا من أستون فيلا الإنجليزي، ليلعب دور البطولة في تتويجه بلقبي دوري روشن وكأس خادم الحرمين الشريفين. غير أن مستويات الجناح الفرنسي تراجعت بشكل كبير خلال الموسم الماضي، ليرتبط اسمه بالانتقال إلى بعض الأندية، كان أبرزها إنتر ميلان، قبل أن يتدخل باير ليفركوزن لضمه. وسيعود صاحب الـ27 عامًا إلى باير ليفركوزن بعد 3 سنوات من الرحيل عنه، حيث لعب له بين عامي 2019 و2023، قبل الانتقال إلى أستون فيلا، الذي رحل منه إلى الاتحاد في ص…

items.title: Kindle users get blindsided by updates that end a popular ebook loophole and toughen DRM
items.summary: Kindle users are getting an unwelcomed surprise through two updates.
items.body: TL;DR Two new updates have arrived that will make Kindle users unhappy. One update toughens Digital Rights Management (DRM) on books on the Kindle Oasis. The other closes a Libby loophole that allowed you to keep book loans past the due date. If you’re an avid ebook reader who uses a Kindle , we have some bad news for you. A couple of changes are rolling out that you probably won’t like. One involves Digital Rights Management (DRM), and the other concerns your Libby book loans. Kindle Oasis DRM Starting with the change to DRM, Amazon is pushing an update to the Kindle Oasis. As reported by The eBook Reader , the update makes it harder to remove DRM from Kindle ebooks. Now most DRM-removal tools will no longer work.

items.title: Google could soon make it easier to ask Gemini to take a look at things
items.summary: Guided Vision could be getting its own accessibility shortcut.
items.body: TL;DR Google is working on a Guided Vision accessibility shortcut that could take users straight into Gemini Live’s Camera mode. The shortcut could add a floating Gemini button or use both volume keys, making Guided Vision much easier to launch on the go. Guided Vision lets Gemini use your camera to read text, translate labels, identify objects, and describe what’s around you, though the new shortcut isn’t functional yet. Google Gemini can already use your smartphone’s camera to tell you what’s in front of you — a feature called Guided Vision — but the problem can be getting to it quickly when you need it on the go. Currently, Google requires you to head to Gemini > Gemini Live > Camera mode to access it. That’s a lot of steps for something you might need quick access to, and Google likely knows that, as we’ve just spotted the tech giant working on a new accessibility shortcut. For what it’s worth, there are ways to head straight to Gemini Live without having to open the Gemini app first. items.title: Facing RCS issues in Google Messages? You’re not alone
items.summary: But there may be some potential solutions floating around.
items.body: TL;DR Some Google Messages users are facing RCS connection issues, particularly on Samsung Galaxy devices. The issue seems to occur only after using the Smart Switch app, with Google saying it may be caused by corrupted cache files. While multiple remedies are currently floating around, not all of them appear to be effective. One of the biggest draws of the Google Messages app is RCS messaging , an upgraded version of SMS that adds features like encryption, read receipts, and media support. So it’s no surprise that it’s the preferred method of communication for most people. It now looks like some are facing trouble connecting to RCS in the app. In a thread on Reddit, a user describes switching over from a Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 6 to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and being unable to connect to RCS , reportedly seeing the error code 3100. A Google rep has since chimed in with a potential remedy, while hinting that this may be due to corrupted cache files that could have snuck through while switching devices via Samsung’s Smart Switch app.

items.body: It’s not the best time to buy a smartphone right now. The RAM crisis has driven up prices and widened the gap between mid-range phones and flagships. It’s harder than ever for manufacturers to offer phones that feel like good value without hiking prices. And while market pundits may argue that buying a premium flagship makes more sense than settling for a watered-down mid-ranger, the Pixel 11 makes a surprisingly strong case for spending less. The base Pixel 11 starts at $899 — $100 more than the Pixel 10 — but still $200 less than the Pixel 11 Pro. And the more time I spend with it, the more I realize that most of what I actually want from a Pixel is already here.

items.title: Someone ported this classic Xbox 360 game to Android, and it runs on budget devices
items.summary: You don't need cutting-edge hardware to play this Skate 3 fan port on your Android device.
items.body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR A developer has released an unofficial Android port of Skate 3. The Xbox 360 game runs smoothly on a mid-tier Retroid handheld, and the developer says it’s playable on the sub-$160 ANBERNIC RG406V. The port is quite buggy at the moment, but the developer has already released a few updates. We’ve seen a raft of Xbox 360 games unofficially ported to PC in recent months, and Skate 3 is one of these titles. The popular skateboarding game received two fan ports a few months back, but what about Android? We now have good news on this front. Developer Buku313 released an unofficial Android port of Skate 3 on GitHub this week, dubbed Skate 3 Mobile . This is a fork of the recent Skate3Recomp project for PC. Unlike many other Xbox 360 ports, which often still emulate the GPU, both of these Skate 3 ports have a native Vulkan renderer. In plain English, you can expect fast performance compared to typical fan ports of many Xbox 360 titles.

items.title: Testing the Galaxy S26 Plus at night exposes flagship smartphone cameras’ biggest mistake
items.summary: Bigger camera sensors still matter, especially when the lights go down.
items.body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority When shopping for the best camera phones in the business, we’re increasingly spoilt for choice, with the best flagships offering multi-sensor setups with huge megapixel counts, wide apertures, long-range zoom, and swathes of other flagship-tier camera technologies. However, move away from the very top-of-the-line camera phones, and it’s all too common to see that slightly cheaper flagships and mid-range phones are stuck with far less sophisticated camera arrays. The Pixel 11 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro are good exceptions to this trend because they share the same hardware as their even more expensive XL and Max siblings, though the regular Pixel 11 and iPhone 17 miss out on some features. The same can’t be said for Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Plus , however, which is a pale imitation of the Ultra. I’ve been dabbling back in with Samsung’s flagship phones in recent weeks and was having trouble putting my finger on exactly why the Plus felt like such a mediocre camera package — until I took another look at the spec sheet.

It is also extending the 50% increased weekly Claude Code limits through August 31. Claude already has a ton of integrations with third-party apps and services. It can also check your Gmail for unread emails, action items, and do a lot more . However, Anthropic is now adding even more capabilities to its Gmail and Google Drive integrations. items.title: Phone displays with ‘beneficial red light’ might be what your strained eyes need
items.summary: The upcoming flagship’s screen will reportedly support the industry-leading BT.2020 ultra-wide color gamut.
items.body: TL;DR According to a prominent leaker, the OPPO Find X10 flagship could offer a display that supports BT.2020, one of the widest color gamuts. Consequently, the tipster claims the Find X10’s display will offer the “highest beneficial red light” courtesy of its upgraded display tech. OPPO is expected to launch the Find X10 series in the fourth quarter, with China getting first dibs on the device, followed by global markets. Display makers have long tried to combat complaints about eye fatigue with hardware solutions, while smartphone brands typically rely on software solutions to reduce harmful blue light emitted by the screen. But every now and then, manufacturers push the envelope with new display tech. OPPO may be the next to join that list. According to leaker Digital Chat Station on Weibo , the display on the company’s Find X10 series will include an “eye-protection substrate” that supports BT.2020, the widest color gamut standard in the industry today. Furthermore, the insider claims that the Find X10’s screen will achieve the “highest beneficial red light and lowest harmful blue light.”

items.body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR Google has updated the Pixel Screenshots app (v1.26.281.05) to add essential date-range and source-filtering options. Users can now sort screenshots by the specific app they were taken in and combine multiple filter criteria simultaneously. The update addresses long-standing complaints about the app’s lack of basic organizational features. Google recently updated the Pixel Screenshots app to switch from exclusively using on-device AI to using cloud-based AI for some of its processing. This change understandably miffed some users , worsened by the app’s rather bare-bones feature set. Google wants to win back some of these users, but it’s now doing so by adding more features to Pixel Screenshots, and frankly, these should have been present from the beginning. The latest Pixel Screenshots app v1.26.281.05 is rolling out to users through the Play Store and brings along the “Filters” feature. Before this update, Pixel Screenshots provided readymade chip-style filters for products, places, promo codes, etc., based on information present in the screenshot, essentially categorizing it.

items.title: OpenAI built a version of ChatGPT that refuses to do your kid’s homework
items.summary: The new ChatGPT for Teens locks down homework shortcuts and AI romance.
items.body: TL;DR OpenAI is launching ChatGPT for Teens with stronger protections enabled by default. Teens get learning-focused tools, while parents get Quiet Hours, settings controls, and limited safety alerts. The move comes as AI creates risks that traditional parental controls weren’t designed to handle. Parents today face a problem that didn’t really exist a few years ago. Today, AI can hold a conversation with a child, respond to sensitive questions, generate content, and potentially become something far more personal than another app on a phone. We’ve already seen how messy that can get: Google’s own AI Search tools have faced scrutiny over the risks they could pose to younger users . In light of these concerns, OpenAI is launching ChatGPT for Teens, a specialized version of its chatbot for 13- to 17-year-olds that prioritizes learning over instant answers while layering in parental controls for added oversight. Rather than sit back and watch, OpenAI is taking a more proactive approach with ChatGPT for Teens. According to the company, the experience applies additional protections around self-harm, eating disorders, violence, dangerous activities, and explicit sexual or graphic content…

Spotify’s editors will also use the feature to give context behind songs added to curated playlists. After adding the new Running Mode and User Notes features, Spotify is introducing yet another feature for its users: Playlist Notes. With it, Spotify hopes to let both users and its team of editors add context to the playlists they curate. The “Playlist Notes” feature is an extension of the “User Notes” feature Spotify introduced late last month. User Notes allowed users to add notes to individual tracks in playlists they owned. However, the streaming platform is now expanding it to cover not just tracks but also audiobooks and podcast episodes that users add to playlists they own or collaborate on.

Rumors over the past couple of years have indicated that Apple is working on a version of the AirPods with built-in cameras. Then, in May, these AI-powered earbuds reached a new company milestone , suggesting a launch wasn’t far away. We’re now gaining additional information about what these AirPods can do, while also potentially getting our first look at the earbuds themselves. items.title: Bizarre YouTube bug is completely wiping out comments and video details, but a fix is coming
items.summary: Exiting full screen leaves a blank void where comments and titles are meant to be.
items.body: TL;DR Google has acknowledged a YouTube iPad bug that erases titles, descriptions, and comments when exiting full screen. The bug likely stems from iPad app version 21.32.4 released last week, though Google has not confirmed the trigger. Affected users can temporarily restore missing UI elements by toggling portrait and landscape mode in full screen. Google has officially acknowledged a widespread full-screen bug in the YouTube iPad app that wipes out video titles, descriptions, channel information, and comment sections entirely. A post in the community forum confirmed that engineering teams are actively investigating the flaw and developing a permanent software fix. The bug began surfacing over the weekend as user reports flooded Reddit and Google’s official support forums . When viewers exit full-screen playback on an iPad, the entire interface region below the video player turns blank. Attempting to start a new video fails to fix the broken layout, as the missing UI carries over from one video to the next within the active app session.

items.body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Fairphone has released the Fairphone Gen 6 Plus, the first model directly available in the US. Previous models in the US were sold via software firm Murena and ran the Google-free /e/OS Android fork. The Fairphone Gen 6 Plus costs $649 or £569. Fairphone first made a splash over a decade ago by offering ethically built, repairable phones . The company has continued this trend over the years while also offering lengthy update commitments. It launched the Fairphone Gen 6 last year, and it’s now offering a mid-gen refresh of sorts. This is the Fairphone Gen 6 Plus, and it’s now officially available in the US. Previous Fairphone models were available in the US via software company Murena and ran the firm’s Google-free /e/OS Android fork. items.title: One UI 9’s new Warranty hub means no more hunting for repair receipts
items.summary: Track warranties, check repair costs, and book tech support directly in Settings.
items.body: TL;DR Samsung has provided more details about the Warranty and care hub that debuted with One UI 9 on its latest foldables. The hub centralizes warranty tracking, diagnostics, and repair booking directly inside Settings. The official rollout confirms new features, including Bixby troubleshooting, ecosystem device management, and side-by-side repair cost estimates. Samsung is finally giving us a closer look at the Warranty and care feature we first spotted hiding in an early One UI 9 build back in March. In a blog post , the company has detailed how the support hub works, revealing a more comprehensive system for checking warranties, diagnosing problems, comparing repair costs, and getting help without leaving the Settings app. We already knew the basic idea. Our earlier teardown found a work-in-progress Warranty and care tool that appeared to bring warranty information, diagnostics, repairs, and customer support together. At the time, though, several features were unfinished. Samsung’s latest explanation fills in some of those blanks and confirms that the feature is intended to become a central destination for Galaxy device care.

items.title: This Gemini Notebook upgrade could completely change how you use shared notebooks
items.summary: Why start from scratch when someone already built the perfect foundation?
items.body: TL;DR Gemini Notebook can now copy entire shared notebooks, including their sources and Studio content, giving you a ready-made starting point to customize. Most Studio creations come along with the copy, including Audio and Video Overviews, Study Guides, Flashcards, Quizzes, Slide Decks, prompts, and custom chat configurations. Copied notebooks are completely independent of the original, while personal notes and chat history stay private. Owners can also disable copying through the “Allow copies” setting. One of the best things about Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) is being able to throw a bunch of information into one place and let Gemini make sense of it. The annoying part is when someone else has already done all that work, and you want to take their notebook, build on it, and make it your own. Google is finally making that possible — you can now copy a notebook along with its sources and Studio content, provided the original owner allows copying. The new notebook is then added to your own library, where you can take what was already built and make it your own.
